content_html:
Walking through Cusco is one of the best ways to feel the essence of the city. Its cobblestone streets, colonial mansions, mysterious alleys and impressive viewpoints make each walk a unique experience. Here we leave you the best short hikes to explore Cusco on foot.

1. San Blas – Sapantiana Walk

Duration: 20-30 min (one way)
Home: Plaza de Armas
Destination: Sapantiana Viewpoint

San Blas is one of the most picturesque neighborhoods in Cusco, famous for its narrow streets, art galleries and bohemian atmosphere. This walk will take you through cobbled alleys, colonial houses with wooden balconies and the beautiful Sapantiana viewpoint, with its colonial style stone aqueduct.

Recommended route:

  • Go up Hatun Rumiyoc Street (where the 12 angle stone is).
  • Explore the Plaza de San Blas and its church.
  • Go down 7 Diablitos Street until you reach the Sapantiana Aqueduct, a perfect place for photos.

The best: Old streets, art workshops and a different viewpoint.

2. Walk Plaza de Armas – Mirador de San Cristóbal

Duration: 15-20 min
Home: Plaza de Armas
Destination: San Cristobal Viewpoint

If you are looking for a short walk but with a spectacular view of the Historic Center, this is ideal. You will go up old stairs and colonial streets until you reach the church of San Cristóbal, where you will have a impressive panoramic of Cusco.

Recommended route:

  • Leave the Plaza de Armas and go up Sweden Street.
  • Take the Resbalosa or Don Bosco slope to reach the viewpoint.
  • Enjoy the view and visit the church of San Cristóbal.

The best: Perfect view of the center of Cusco without going too far.

3. Walk to the Borreguitos Viewpoint

Duration: 20-25 min
Home: Saint Blaise
Destination: Borreguitos Viewpoint

One of the least known viewpoints in Cusco, but with an incredible view and little influx of tourists. This elevated point offers you a unique angle of the city with a calmer atmosphere.

Recommended route:

  • Go up from San Blas along Tandapata Street.
  • Cross towards the San Cristóbal area and follow the uphill trails.
  • Enjoy the viewpoint in complete tranquility.

The best: A hidden corner with unparalleled views.

4. Walk to the Cristo Blanco Viewpoint

Duration: 35-40 min
Home: Plaza de Armas
Destination: Cristo Blanco Viewpoint

This is one of the most popular tours for those who want a 360° view of Cusco. The climb is a little demanding, but it is worth it when you reach the statue of Cristo Blanco.

Recommended route:

  • Leave the Plaza de Armas and go up Resbalosa or Don Bosco Street.
  • Arrive in San Cristóbal and follow the road to Sacsayhuamán.
  • From there, climb up to Cristo Blanco and enjoy the view.

The best: The best panoramic view of Cusco and the proximity to Sacsayhuamán.

5. Plaza de Armas Walk – Calle 7 Culebras

Duration: 10-15 min
Home: Plaza de Armas
Destination: 7 Culebras Street

This is a hike short but full of history and mystery. 7 Culebras Street is a cobblestone passage with murals of snakes carved in stone, a vestige of the Inca and colonial influence in the city.

Recommended route:

  • From the Plaza de Armas, walk towards Loreto Street (between Inca walls).
  • Arrive at Plazoleta Nazarenas and look for 7 Culebras Street.
  • Explore the stone carvings and colonial atmosphere of the passage.

The best: A quick walk with hidden details of Cusco history.

Tips to enjoy hiking in Cusco

Bring water and sunscreen, the weather in Cusco can change quickly.
Wear comfortable shoes, many streets are cobbled. You can buy it in Cusco itself.
Avoid night walks in remote areas for security.
If you want to avoid height, walk slowly and take breaks.

Which of these hikes do you want to do first?

Cusco is a perfect city to explore on foot, with its natural viewpoints and streets full of history. Whether you are looking for a tour short and relaxed or a rise with stunning viewsThere are options for all tastes.
